title: Grateful Dead Live at Dupont Gymnasium M.I.T. on 1970-05-07
lineage: AudMC > ? > 7 inch Reel > DAT > HD > Soundforge > SHN

ai_review.summary: A rough audience tape of a legendary early‑70 show, marred by hiss and muffled mix but rescued by an incendiary Lovelight and scorching early‑set jams.
ai_review.review: Despite the grainy AUD recording that leaves some instruments buried in hiss, this performance shines thanks to a monster Lovelight, fiery second‑set openings (Good Lovin', Cold Rain, Easy Wind) and a classic Cryptical > The Other One > Cosmic Charlie sequence. Jerry’s guitar work is repeatedly praised – from an explosive solo that “shreds” to his steel‑guitar cameo with NRPS – making the show a must‑listen for fans of the young, adventurous Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviewers celebrate the musical performance and highlight several standout moments; recording quality is consistently described as poor to fair but not enough to outweigh the show's strength.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Heavy tape hiss, muffled instrument isolation and occasional drop‑outs make the audio challenging; vocals remain audible and the overall energy comes through despite the lo‑fi mix.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Cosmic Charlie
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set structure (acoustic, NRPS with Jerry on steel, electric) showcases the band's youthful adventurousness; acoustic set sets a relaxed tone, the NRPS interlude adds novelty, and the electric second set bursts with high‑energy improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note his incendiary solo early in the second electric set and laud his steel‑guitar work with NRPS, calling it beautiful and ‘shredding.’
